findings.title: Malformed checksum line gives opaque error
findings.message: A blank or malformed line in a checksum file makes the unpack raise ValueError with the unhelpful message 'not enough values to unpack'. A blank trailing line in the middle of the file, for example, also fails this way. The result is a confusing error rather than a clear validation message.
findings.suggestion: Skip empty lines and validate that the separator is present before splitting.

fix.after:
require('  ' in line, 'malformed checksum line')
        value, name = line.split('  ', 1)

findings.title: extractfile may return None; unhandled AttributeError
findings.message: The size check relies on the tar header, which is trusted as given. The member is then read whole into memory. Reading a member that is much larger than its header claims is not a realistic case for a well-formed tar, but extractfile can return None, which would raise AttributeError. That exception is not in the caught list, so the script ends with a traceback instead of the clean failure message.
findings.suggestion: Check that extractfile did not return None and fail through require(). Also add AttributeError to the caught exceptions, or read in bounded chunks.
findings.evidence:
stream = archive.extractfile(member)
            require(hashlib.sha256(stream.read()).hexdigest() == record['sha256'], 'evidence member checksum mismatch')

fix.before:
stream = archive.extractfile(member)
            require(hashlib.sha256(stream.read()).hexdigest() == record['sha256'], 'evidence member checksum mismatch')
fix.after:
stream = archive.extractfile(member)
            require(stream is not None, 'unreadable evidence member')
            require(hashlib.sha256(stream.read(16 * 1024 * 1024 + 1)).hexdigest() == record['sha256'], 'evidence member checksum mismatch')
